dogs cant swim apparently

under the shed
Describe a very small place from inside it.

Dust in the mouth first. Then the undersides of the boards, each dark ring of a knot looking closer than it should. I had thought there would be room to turn my head. There isn't. The kitten has gone quiet and I can't see beyond the pipe. With one cheek flat against the earth I can hear traffic through the ground, a heavy soft noise, quite different to being above it. I push the saucer ahead of me. It tips. Milk soaks into the soil before I can reach it. Now my elbow is stuck against something sharp and I have to go backwards.
bare patch
Describe what you can actually see, without making a story.

four wet paving stones. grass in three cracks, no grass in the fourth. somebody has dragged a chair here. the lines are white and powdery even with the water on them. a tiny red thing moving on my wrist and gone before i can look properly
thinning them out
A small practical task becomes difficult.

I know you are meant to pull some out. Every ten centimetres says the packet. But they're all perfectly healthy and I have got as far as one. That one is on the edge of the bed going limp. I could move it. The point was not to have so many, though. Last year the carrots were thin as wire. We ate them anyway. I have a tray somewhere, maybe I can move half into that. Need more soil then. And a place to put the tray.
August, no rain
Imagine that one ordinary natural process stops.

The bees stop at the same place in the air. Not all together, one after another, as though each has reached a small invisible pane of glass. By noon there are twenty hovering over the dry pond. I put my hand through. Nothing. The wings are still working, making a sound so high it almost isn't a sound. I bring the hose but the water runs sideways at that spot and wets my shoes. I wish Daniel was here because he would try something sensible before being frightened. I have turned off the tap and the water is still coming.
away game
Write a scene in which someone is accused of cheating.

They said we brought an older player but Samir is fourteen he is just tall. The other coach wanted his birth certifcate like he would have it in his socks. Then Samir takes his boots off and says hes not playing. I tell him put them back on we need him. He says thats all anyone says.

He walks right past the bus and out the gates. Coach sent me after him. When I caught him he looked at the captains band first before my face. I took it off. Now I have to say something.
one bounce
A game changes its rules halfway through.

We were playing one bounce in the car park and Leon said the white line was out. It wasnt out before when his ball went over it. I said fine then the drain is out as well. Soon everyhing was out and we were standing in these little spaces trying not to move our feet. Then the ball went on the roof. We stared at it for ages. Leon found a stick that was like a metre long for a roof about four metres high and tried anyway. I was laughing so so much I didnt see the owner come out, he thought we had been throwing stones and he grabs Leon's arm and I stopped laughing then.
Relay 8
A signal arrives with a physical side effect.

At 04:12 the receiver spat gravel. Real gravel, three pieces, hot enough to blister the desk. There isn't an opening in the casing wide enough for them. I unplugged it and got the same transmission, the voice counting down from eight. Seven. Six. I put the whole unit in the sink. Five. It isn't a bomb, I kept thinking, a bomb wouldn't need you to hear it. Four. The drain started sucking air. I could see daylight through it, a square of orange sky below the U bend. Three. I went to get my camera which was such a stupid thing to do because when I came back the sink was empty and the countdown was coming from my mouth.

extinction test
A machine begins making a sound nobody taught it.

The sample says a word. We replay it nine times, clean the filter, try another headset. Same word. Not English. It sounds like 'allow' until you listen to it thinking 'below' and then it sounds like that. Hesh wants to publish. I want to know why the waveform is exactly the outline of the hill outside. He says I am seeing patterns. I ask him to look out the window. The hill wasn't there yesterday.
South of the Glass
A young traveller must carry something dangerous.

The egg was getting heavy. It had been small enough to fit in Eda's coat when she stole it, now she had to roll it along the road and it left a groove in the dust. She kept saying sorry to whatever was inside. At the river the ferrryman wouldnt take her. He could hear tapping. Eda could hear it too but she said it was stones in her shoes. That wasn't a good lie, she had no shoes. The egg rolled a little closer to the water by itself. Across the river the trees bent backwards all at once, and the ferryman dropped his rope. She jumped in his boat while he was looking. There was room for her or the egg. She hadn't thought about that.
first bridge
Tell a fairy tale from the youngest sibling’s point of view.

My brothers went over first and the bridge ate them. I don't mean a troll under it, I mean the actual bridge folded up at both ends like a sandwich. It was flat again when I got there. Their packs lay on the bank with the straps cut. I threw a stone and nothing happened. I threw another one and it came back. So I sat down. Gran says everything alive gets hungry and everything hungry makes a mistake eventually. I had three apples, a wool blanket and a knife too blunt to peel with. It was going to be a long wait. By dark the bridge had moved six feet nearer me.

There is a wolf but he doesnt want to eat anybody. He wants to find his mum. I think wolves leave their mums though. Maybe he is still little. He finds the red cloak caught on a branch and smells soap which he has never smelled before
The orchard raid
Someone has to choose what to rescue.

They came in on the west wind with burning nets. Marra lowered the children down the well on the bell rope. She went last. Halfway down she remembered the seed book on the table. Without it they wouldn't know which fruit made you sleep. She couldn't climb back without dragging the children against the wall. She let go. Above them somebody tried the lid. Her son was about to call for help so she covered his mouth. He thought it was his father. She could see him trying to say it.
Second speech
A family celebration does not go as rehearsed.

Greta had been asked to say a few words about her father. She had written three pages, then one, then a sentence on the back of the menu. By the time her brother handed her the microphone she had spilled wine on that. The room was waiting. She could see her father leaning back, smiling already, ready to receive whatever version of himself she could make pleasant enough for the occasion. She said that he had taught her to drive. Her brother nodded, encouraging. She said that he used to get out at the traffic lights and walk home if she stalled. Someone laughed because they thought she was building to a joke. She looked at her father. He had put his glass down. Now she could remember all three pages.
back row
Describe a social event without resolving the awkwardness.

I didn't recognise the bride. There were pictures at the entrance but they had been taken in bright sun, with her hair down; the person coming towards me was pale and very young. I told her she looked beautiful. She said thank you and asked how I knew her husband. Her husband had once asked me to leave my own wedding for him. It was an old story and a foolish one, and in the church I had found myself enjoying the flowers and hoping these two would be happy. I said we had worked together. That was also true. She took my arm and said there was someone she wanted me to meet, so I left my coat on the chair and followed her.

the other route
Walk towards a place you have been avoiding.

I can get to the hospital three different ways and I have begun to think choosing the right one might affect what happens there. I know that isn't sensible. Last Tuesday I went by the canal and the news was good, today there is a barrier across the towpath and I am standing in front of it arguing with nobody. A man in a yellow jacket says the bank has slipped. I ask how long the diversion is. He says ten minutes. I say I don't have ten minutes though I left an hour early specifically so I would have time to sit outside and not go in. He is waiting for me to move. Behind him a duck is standing in the middle of the broken path, and I wish I could explain this without sounding like a person who needs help herself.

route notes
Write down a walk as you remember it.

left at the pharmacy except it isn't one now. two dogs in an upstairs window. a woman carrying a shovel horizontally. the smell from the drains and then suddenly bread.

I wanted a story about following a stranger but I didn't follow anyone. Got a bun, walked to the old pool, saw they had filled it with rubble and came back. The bun had coconut which I don't like. Bought it anyway because the girl had already picked it up and I couldn't be bothered saying no.
the bells started early
A familiar city changes while you are walking through it.

At the first corner the street has a different name. I keep going because names change. At the second corner the road drops steeply towards water that wasn't there this morning. I can see my office on the far side, fourth-floor window still open, my cardigan on the chair. There are people down on the bank holding their phones above their heads. None of them are looking at the water, they're trying to get a signal. I try mine too. It says I'm seven kilometres away from where I am. Behind me the bells start again and this time the buildings on my left lean, very slowly, as if somebody is pulling the street from underneath them.
Survey 14
A map is accurate in a way it should not be.

We survey the cellar twice. North wall 4.2 metres. South wall 4.2. Distance between them, six. Outside the entire house is only five metres deep. I check the laser against the tape. Same readings. Nina says perhaps the cellar extends under the pavement. It doesn't. I draw the outline on the floor in chalk, using the upstairs measurements, and there's a strip of dark concrete left over. No pipes, no drain. Just the extra metre. Nina puts one foot across the chalk line. Her radio cuts out. She takes it back. The radio works. We agree not to step over again. Then she tells me she has left her tape on the other side and I can see it moving away from us.
A way through
A character escapes by noticing the shape of a building.

The stair reaches a wall. Felix is behind me saying go go go and I can't tell him there's nowhere. I push and the plaster gives. A room beyond, chairs facing the other way, coats over all the backs. No people. We crawl under a table. Footsteps stop outside. A hand reaches through the hole. It is wearing my watch.
who invited him
A family meal is interrupted by an unexpected guest.

Mum opened the door with flour all up her arms and just said no. My uncle was outside holding a watermellon, in November, I dont know where he got it. He said can I come in and she said the last time you came in you took the television. He said he borrowed it. Mum looked behind her at me and I pretended I was very busy chopping onions even though there were no onions left. He put the watermelon in the doorway so she couldnt close it. That made her laugh which made her angrier. I said I'll cut it up and she snapped don't you dare, then my brother came downstairs and said uncle! and ran straight past both of us.

I made one huge dumpling with the last bit of dough. Amal looked at it and started laughing so hard she sat on the floor. We'd been there since six. I sat down too.
